activities.name: Polygraph
activities.howto: Read the statement. The team decides: true or false?

cards.q: Netflix started out as a DVD-by-mail rental company.
The very first text message ever sent read 'Merry Christmas.'
There are more possible games of chess than atoms in the observable universe.
TikTok absorbed an app called Musical.ly to break into the US market.
Bitcoin has an unlimited supply.
cards.note: It's capped at 21 million coins.

cards.q: The first iPhone was released in 2007.
Emoji were invented in the United States.
cards.note: They were invented in Japan in the late 1990s.

cards.q: The New York Times bought Wordle.
Google was originally called BackRub.
The word 'podcast' comes from the iPod.
Zoom was founded during the COVID-19 pandemic.
cards.note: It was founded in 2011.

cards.q: The Bluetooth logo is built from two Scandinavian runes.
In most US states, rideshare drivers are legally employees of the app company.
cards.note: They're generally independent contractors.

cards.q: 'Doomscrolling' has been added to major dictionaries.
Spotify pays artists about one dollar per stream.
cards.note: It's a fraction of a cent.

cards.q: The Mars rover Perseverance landed in 2021.
QR codes were invented in the 2010s for restaurant menus.
cards.note: They were invented in Japan in 1994 for tracking car parts.

cards.q: Airbnb started when its founders rented out air mattresses in their own apartment.
Electric cars have more moving parts in the drivetrain than gas cars.
Amazon started out selling only books.
'Barbie' and 'Oppenheimer' were released in theaters on the same day.
Google's parent company is named Alphabet.
YouTube was founded by former PayPal employees.
Slack was originally built as an internal tool at a video game company.
The James Webb Space Telescope orbits the Earth, just like Hubble.
cards.note: It orbits the Sun, about a million miles out.

cards.q: Duolingo's mascot is an owl.
'Rizz' is short for 'charisma.'
Nvidia got its start making graphics cards for video games.
The @ symbol appeared on typewriters before computers existed.
Wikipedia's articles are written by paid staff writers.
cards.note: It's written and edited by unpaid volunteers.

cards.q: The 'S' in HTTPS stands for 'secure.'
'Wi-Fi' is an abbreviation of 'Wireless Fidelity.'
cards.note: It's a brand name a marketing firm invented — it doesn't stand for anything.

cards.q: Incognito mode hides your browsing from your internet provider.
cards.note: It only stops your own browser from saving the history.

cards.q: Bitcoin transactions are anonymous and untraceable.
cards.note: Every transaction is recorded on a public ledger.

cards.q: Nvidia now earns more from data centers than from gaming.
5G networks caused the COVID-19 pandemic.
Electric cars produce zero emissions across their full life cycle.
cards.note: Manufacturing and grid electricity both carry emissions.

cards.q: Most of the world's internet traffic travels through undersea cables.
Signal and WhatsApp both use end-to-end encryption by default.
Deleting a file immediately erases it from the drive.
cards.note: It usually just marks the space as reusable.

cards.q: TikTok's feed mainly shows you content from accounts you follow.
cards.note: The main feed is recommendation-driven, not follow-driven.

cards.q: The EU passed a law requiring USB-C charging ports on new phones.
Solar is now cheaper than new coal power in most of the world.
A blockchain has to be public to work at all.
cards.note: Private and permissioned chains exist.

cards.q: Video streaming accounts for the majority of internet bandwidth.
Text-message two-factor codes are the most secure option available.
cards.note: An authenticator app or hardware key is stronger — SMS can be intercepted.

cards.q: Amazon's cloud business is more profitable than its retail business.
Modern AI language models are programmed with explicit grammar rules.
cards.note: They learn statistical patterns from text instead.

cards.q: The James Webb Space Telescope observes mainly in infrared.
Apple takes a cut of most purchases made inside App Store apps.
There are more mobile phone subscriptions in the world than there are people.
The first computer programmer is generally considered to have been a woman.
cards.note: Ada Lovelace, in the 1840s.

cards.q: Training a large AI model uses about as much electricity as a household does in a week.
cards.note: It's orders of magnitude more than that.

cards.q: Most crypto trading volume happens on decentralized exchanges.
cards.note: Centralized exchanges still dominate.

cards.q: Fertility rates have been falling in nearly every country on Earth.
Extreme poverty worldwide has fallen by more than half since 1990.
The word 'robot' comes from a Czech play.
cards.note: Karel Capek's 'R.U.R.', 1920.

cards.q: Email existed before the World Wide Web.
A QR code still scans with up to about 30% of it damaged.
cards.note: Error correction is built into the format.

cards.q: GPS satellites have to correct for Einstein's relativity to stay accurate.
The internet and the World Wide Web are two names for the same thing.
cards.note: The web is one service running on top of the internet.

cards.q: Nvidia was founded in the 1990s.
The screen is the most expensive component in a typical smartphone.
cards.note: The processor and other silicon usually cost more.

cards.q: Lithium is the scarcest material in an electric car battery.
cards.note: Cobalt and nickel supply are the tighter constraints.

cards.q: The average person checks their phone fewer than 20 times a day.
Streaming a movie uses more energy than driving to a video store would have.
Bitcoin's annual energy use is comparable to that of a mid-sized country.
The @ symbol was picked for email addresses partly because it was rarely used.
Moore's Law is a law of physics.
cards.note: It's an observed trend, and an industry target.

cards.q: The first webcam was set up to watch a coffee pot.
cards.note: The Trojan Room coffee pot at Cambridge.

cards.q: Vine videos were capped at six seconds.
MySpace let you set a song that played automatically on your profile.
Blockbuster had the chance to buy Netflix and turned it down.
The Wii shipped with Wii Sports in most regions.
A Snapchat streak counts consecutive days two people have snapped each other.
The first Harry Potter film came out in the 1990s.
cards.note: It was released in 2001.

cards.q: 'Gangnam Style' was the first YouTube video to pass a billion views.
The iPod was released before the iPhone.
Angry Birds started life as a console game.
cards.note: It launched on mobile in 2009.

cards.q: Disney bought Club Penguin.
The Ice Bucket Challenge raised over $100 million for ALS research.
Flappy Bird was pulled from app stores by its own creator.
Minecraft was created by a Swedish developer.
cards.note: Markus 'Notch' Persson.

cards.q: The Harlem Shake videos all used a track by a producer called Baauer.
Twitter's original character limit was 140.
YouTube was originally built as a video dating site.
The 'Distracted Boyfriend' meme is a stock photo shot in Spain.
cards.note: Barcelona.

cards.q: Facebook bought Instagram for around a billion dollars.
The blue-and-black versus white-and-gold dress argument happened in 2015.
Rick Astley wrote 'Never Gonna Give You Up' himself.
cards.note: It was written by the production trio Stock Aitken Waterman.

cards.q: The Beatles came from Liverpool.
Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon.
The first Star Wars film came out in the 1970s.
Elvis Presley was known as the King of Pop.
cards.note: He was the King of Rock and Roll.

cards.q: Cassette tapes came before CDs.
The Rubik's Cube was invented in the 1980s.
cards.note: It was invented in 1974.

cards.q: The Berlin Wall came down in 1989.
Betamax beat VHS in the home video format war.
cards.note: VHS won.

cards.q: Woodstock was held in the town of Woodstock.
cards.note: It was held on a farm in Bethel, New York.

cards.q: Sputnik was launched by the United States.
cards.note: It was launched by the Soviet Union.

cards.q: The first handheld mobile phone call was made in the 1970s.
MTV's first music video was 'Video Killed the Radio Star.'
